title: Void Ending in a Trine to Jupiter
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 4, Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The trine is the best of the aspects, the one the doctrine uses to tie the Moon to the fortunes. The text grades it as perfect friendship, because the signs it joins are of one element and gaze at each other in full agreement; works meant to endure are founded with the Moon fixed, and the lord of her house regarding her in trine or sextile.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a trine to Jupiter, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his temperate growth. Jupiter is the Great Fortune, hot and humid and temperate, the source of growing power: law, legality, jurisprudence, wisdom, the interpretation of dreams, and the ready winning of requests. His benevolence fits clergymen, kings, and lords; tin is his metal, the emerald and every shining white stone are his, and his animals are the beautiful and harmless ones once used for sacrifice. Set in the ascendant or at mid-heaven, the text says, he and Venus together rectify the Moon's misfortunes.
